rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Header at line 30, `## Your nag writes the verifier`, asserts an unqualified causal claim (the nag produces the verifier). The maintainer's own 2026-08-14 correction note (a), quoted in the body above the fence, explicitly REJECTS that exact claim: the removed sentence read 'Your nag is a spec, arriving one worry at a time. Each one names a check the session should have carried with it' — Antti's own words call this 'contradicts... the agent encodes from evidence.' The corrected body (lines 34-36, read fresh this session) now says 'Hold that worry beside the artefact. Where the run bears it out, it names your first check. Where it doesn't, the artefact wins: it saw the session and you didn't' — a conditional, artefact-adjudicated claim, not an unconditional 'writes.' The header was not touched by the 2026-08-14 correction (only the body prose is quoted/discussed in that maintainer note) and still names the stronger, now-disavowed claim. HARM CHECK (mandatory clause): this rule exists to stop a header asserting more than the body supports, because a crisp header is easier to believe than the qualified prose beneath it — exactly what self-study/deck-cold reading rewards (§4's own diagnostic: 'cover the bullets; the header still names the ONE thing the student walks away holding'). The harm is present, not theoretical: a skim reader retains 'my nag writes the verifier,' which is precisely the epistemically-charitable-to-self-report belief Phase 1 of `diagnose-and-resend` teaches the student to distrust ('assume about 10% of the account misrepresents the run') and precisely what Antti's own correction rationale names as the fault. No maintainer accept-note covers the header specifically — the 2026-08-14 note discusses only the body sentence removed.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Rename the header to match the corrected body's adjudication move rather than the disavowed 'nag writes' claim — e.g. something closer to 'Weigh your nag against the artefact' or 'Your nag, checked' — author's call, not a prescribed replacement.
